title: Moving to New Orleans and buying his first drums
summary: He moved to New Orleans at about 16, lived with his grandmother and Uncle Oscar, and bought a $25 secondhand set from a pawnshop with wages from a $9-a-week job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Did you play up in Thibodeau or when did you move down? How old were you when you moved down to New Orleans? I was about 16 years old. Um, had you played up there? When did you start on drums? I know as you say you started really when you were five years old. I guess you started in your interest in it, but when did you actually start playing it that you could say you were really a drummer?
I started when I was about 17 years old in New Orleans.
After you moved down, you didn't really play drums up there in the group then?
No, I never did play in New Orleans. I mean in Thibodeau I played in New Orleans.
So you moved down here? Did you have lessons when you moved down?

Well when I came down from Thibodeau to New Orleans, I moved with my grandmother. And she lived with her son Oscar Giles. And I told him I thought I had interest that I would like to play a drum. So I worked at the Crescent Steen Partridge Way. I was getting nine dollars a week. I decided I wanted to buy a drum. So he'd take me on Ramport and Padres in a pawn shop. That's where I bought my first set of drums for a second hand. I paid 25 dollars for the set. Things were cheap at that time.
They were a lot cheaper then than them now.
